item.title: Looking for Fulfillment
item.description:
Looking for Fulfillment Philip T. Mistlberger

Source: TW

Author: Philip T. Mistlberger

Philp Mistlberger’s new website is coming soon.

Link to entry on Advaita Sites page.

Link to listing on Recommended Books page.

The following is extracted from the above book, ‘A Natural Awakening: Realizing the True Self in Everyday Life’, which can be purchased from Philip’s website. N.B. Only a few copies left!

Everyone is searching for their “true being”—but almost always, this search is not recognized for what it really is and is rather only vaguely understood as a longing or desire for some sort of completion or fulfillment. This longing and desire usually gets directed outwardly, into the content of the world. It becomes the search for status, approval, love, family, accomplishment, possessions, fame, power, and so on.

item.title: Spiritual Experiences
item.description:
Spiritual Experiences Philip T. Mistlberger

Source: TW

Author: Philip T. Mistlberger

Philp Mistlberger’s new website is coming soon.

Link to entry on Advaita Sites page.

Link to listing on Recommended Books page.

The following is extracted from the above book, ‘A Natural Awakening: Realizing the True Self in Everyday Life’, which can be purchased from Philip’s website. N.B. Only a few copies left!

The longing for freedom eventually directs us to set out on a path— usually called “the spiritual path .” The basis of this path is the intention to realize truth. The path actually goes from nowhere to nowhere, in the sense that what we are really doing is re-discovering our true nature—a true nature that is already the case, underlying the layer of dust created by our minds. But unfortunately the spiritual path is rarely used in this way. Usually it becomes a lengthy, drawn out, progressive affair.
